# Mohammed Elmahfoudi

> Mohammed Elmahfoudi — software engineer building backend systems, APIs, and containerized infrastructure with Python, TypeScript, and C++.

I build backend systems, production APIs, and containerized infrastructure. From HTTP servers in C++ to full-stack platforms in Python and TypeScript, I enjoy understanding how things work from the ground up.

Currently: now · backend developer @ SHBM INF Platform.
Based in: Morocco.

## Projects

- [Webserv — HTTP Server from Scratch](https://github.com/maelmahf/Webserv): Built an HTTP/1.1 server in C++98 with a single-threaded, non-blocking poll() event loop. Supports virtual hosts, location-based routing, asynchronous CGI execution, uploads, persistent connections, and HTTP range requests.
- [Inception — Containerized Infrastructure](https://github.com/maelmahf/inception): Orchestrated NGINX, WordPress, MariaDB, and Redis with Docker Compose. Configured TLS, isolated service networking, and persistent volumes, with Adminer and Portainer for administration.
- [Minishell — Unix Shell](https://github.com/maelmahf/mini_shel): A shell implementation in C with an execution tree, environment-variable expansion, wildcard expansion, quote handling, heredoc handling, and signal management.
- [Philosophers — Concurrency Simulation](https://github.com/maelmahf/Philo): A dining philosophers simulation in C exploring threads, shared state, mutex synchronization, meal timing, and monitoring.
- [Gymbot — Booking Automation](https://github.com/maelmahf/book): A Python automation project that books recurring gym sessions. Includes Docker-based deployment and scheduled execution on Railway.
- [Cub3D](https://github.com/maelmahf/Cub3D): A C graphics project from the 42 curriculum.
- [Push_swap](https://github.com/maelmahf/Push_swap): A C sorting project from the 42 curriculum, built around stack operations.
- [Pipex — Command Pipelines](https://github.com/maelmahf/PIPEX): Recreates command pipelines in C, connecting commands through Unix pipes.
- [So_long — MiniLibX Game](https://github.com/maelmahf/so_long): A small game written in C using the MiniLibX graphics library.
- [C++ Modules 00–09](https://github.com/maelmahf/CPP00-09): A collection of C++ curriculum modules and programming exercises.
- [Libft — C Library](https://github.com/maelmahf/Libft): A personal C library developed as part of the 42 curriculum.
- [Ft_printf](https://github.com/maelmahf/Printf): A C implementation of formatted output from the 42 curriculum.
- [Get Next Line](https://github.com/maelmahf/Get-Next-Line): A C utility for reading input one line at a time.
- Ft_Transcendence — Full-Stack Web Platform: Built a platform with Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and Docker. Implemented candidate and recruiter roles, JWT sessions, protected routing, an AI-powered recommendation API, and recruiter offer management with live UI updates.
- [Sahtek — Web Interface](https://github.com/maelmahf/Sahtek): A web interface with a landing page, login page, and dashboard, built with HTML and supporting assets.

# About me

From systems programming to backend services — my path, my projects, and the questions behind them.

I'm **Mohammed Elmahfoudi**, a software engineer based in Morocco. I build backend services, explore systems programming, and connect the two through projects that take me from memory and sockets to APIs and infrastructure.

I like understanding what happens behind an abstraction. Writing an HTTP server in C++ makes a request feel different when you later handle it in Next.js. Building a shell makes processes, pipes, and signals more than concepts in a textbook. That connection between the foundations and the finished product shapes the way I learn and build.

## From the foundations up

My path started with a DUT in Computer Science at Ecole Supérieure de Technologie in Kénitra. I continued at **1337 Coding School, part of the 42 Network**, where project-based learning has pushed me to turn ideas into working programs.

Along the way, I've worked on a Unix shell, a concurrent philosophers simulation, an HTTP/1.1 server, and a containerized web infrastructure. Each project asks a different question: how do you manage memory, coordinate shared state, handle several clients, or keep services connected?

I'm also studying data engineering with **ALX Africa**, expanding into ETL, data modelling, and cloud architecture.

## Building for people

On the **SHBM INF Platform at UM6P**, I work on backend services for student and administrative workflows. My work includes REST APIs, JWT-based authentication, role-based access, and database query optimization. It's where implementation details meet practical needs: who can access a resource, how data moves, and how a service responds under load.

My full-stack work includes **Ft_Transcendence**, a platform built with Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, and Docker, with candidate and recruiter roles, offer management, and an AI-powered recommendation API.

Beyond code, the **UM6P Explorer Program and MIT Sandbox mentorship** gave me experience developing a healthcare accessibility prototype and testing it with more than 20 users. It brought another question into the process: does what we're building solve a problem for the person using it?

## The tools I reach for

For systems work, I use **C and C++**. For backend services and automation, I work with **Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript**, using tools such as FastAPI, NestJS, and Next.js API routes.

I use **PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB** for data, and **Docker, Linux, NGINX, and GitHub Actions** to configure and run services. When a project needs a frontend, I work with **React, HTML, and CSS**.

The interesting part is how those pieces fit together: a clear API, a useful data model, and infrastructure that supports the application.

## Let's connect

If you're building backend services, working on infrastructure, or have a project where my background could help, I'd be happy to talk.

[Email me](mailto:mohammedelmahfoudi2004@gmail.com) · [Explore my GitHub](https://github.com/maelmahf) · [Connect on LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/maelmahf)
